title: Overnight Guests
short: A good guest agrees on dates, follows the house routine, keeps their space tidy, offers to help, and sends a thank-you afterward; a good host gives towels, a key and a plan.
trouble: Learners extend a stay without asking or expect to be entertained every hour. A clear arrival and departure date helps everyone.

blocks.html: An overnight visit is hosting stretched over days. Host and guest share a home for a while, and small courtesies on both sides keep the visit happy.
A good guest agrees on dates ahead, follows the house routine, keeps their space tidy, offers to help, and sends a thank-you afterward. A good host gives towels, a key and a plan.

Sharing a home means sharing routines: meal times, the bathroom, quiet hours. A clear arrival and departure date lets the host plan work and meals. A guest who fits in with the household, tidies up and helps out lightens the host's load. A host who sets out towels and explains the plan spares the guest from having to ask for every small thing.

head: The guest
The host
rows: Agrees on arrival and departure dates
Offers clear dates and a plan for the visit
Explains the routine: meals, quiet hours, the key
Makes the bed and keeps the room tidy
Sets out towels, sheets and space for a suitcase
Offers to help with meals and dishes
Lets the guest have some time to rest

blocks.title: Staying longer
blocks.q: Leo is visiting his friend Omar for the weekend and would like to stay until Tuesday. What should he do?
steps: The dates were agreed ahead; changing them is a request, not an announcement.
He asks early and makes it easy to say no: "Would it be all right if I stayed until Tuesday? No worries if not."
If Omar hesitates, Leo keeps the original plan.
blocks.a: Ask early, and make it easy to say no.

blocks.title: Morning routine
blocks.q: At Rosa's home, the family eats breakfast at 7:30. Hana is a late sleeper. What should she do?
steps: She fits in with the house routine while she is a guest.
She sets an alarm and joins breakfast, or asks the night before if it's all right to sleep in.
blocks.a: Follow the routine, or ask ahead.

cards.why: Ask ahead; the host may have plans.

cards.text: Expecting to be entertained every hour
cards.why: A host needs time to rest, too.

cards.text: Sending a thank-you note after the visit

blocks.html: Extending a stay without asking, or expecting to be entertained every hour. A clear arrival and departure date helps everyone, and a guest who can enjoy some quiet time is a gift to the host.
